contracts.invariant: Only the current mutation generation and comparison identity may publish a refresh or authorize a hunk; whole-file discards must revalidate the selected discardable files. List transactions publish one complete ordered selection of raw bytes and staging sides. Unchanged selection preserves capture; genuine selection changes and the exact caller raw-path set control discard authority. Background worktree discovery restores sidebar selection without replacing content mounted by an inspector or presenter. Prune authority is bound to the approved preview's administrative registrations and revalidated at writer admission; changed candidates require an updated preview and a new confirmation. Sidebar row restoration refreshes controls and preserves local-branch reference actions without changing mounted content or the browsed revision. Worktree callbacks and deferred confirmations retain their originating window, repository, service and presentation generation; closing or replacing an owner revokes authority even when the same objects are restored. Expected cancellation is silent while genuine current-owner failures remain observable. Repair and prune consent ignore HEAD-only changes but remain sensitive to exact links, lock and availability metadata, administrative identities, executable context and raw Git reports. Explicit History adopts the selected canonical checkout's newest captured revision; passive synchronization preserves its authoritative revision object and mounted content. Lifecycle menu actions use the clicked checkout even when several checkouts share a branch. Owner revocation cancels pending consent and publication while already-admitted checked writes drain through captured-context reconciliation. Operation-owned reconciliation retires earlier ordinary discoveries before they can republish stale records. Pure context checks do not restart capability probes; rejected queued requests coalesce a capability reprobe after admission release and never replay the write. Ownership evidence failures retain valid records and their original cause; stale ownership requires fresh discovery and a new request. Retired discoveries skip ownership scanning. Reclaim consent keeps both Return and Escape bound to cancellation. Fixture drainage delivers clients sequentially and drains the writer again after pane producers finish; revoked discard eligibility cannot reuse prior approval. Hiding, minimizing, or changing foreground windows does not revoke presentation authority: queued errors and repair/prune consent wait until the user returns to the original visible active key window without activating or restoring it. Close, repository or window replacement revokes authority. Deferred consent receives fresh single-use evidence after a genuine wait and is revalidated at confirmation; immediately available consent does not incur another inventory. Earlier invalidations are satisfied by owned reconciliation, while concurrent events and failed reconciliation retain one bounded recovery. Retained stale snapshots expose an accessible warning and Refresh action independently of row equality. Worktree removal rereads current inventory at FIFO admission and compares it with the original approved row; missing initial inventory also requires an owned read before any ordinary mutation. Changed or missing removal evidence rejects the request without adopting refreshed consent. Removal approval additionally binds HEAD OID, exact symbolic reference and detached state. Every owned preflight retires ordinary generations even when it rejects or fails. Inventory rows, flags and status publish coherently; status-only updates retain sidebar object identities. Style selection only prepares a plan; every repair write follows explicit approval of its fresh complete target list. A consumed-preview refresh failure remains terminal through repeated presentation waits. Passive current-branch, reference and settings selection restoration preserves already-mounted content; explicit branch selection remains a navigation action. Queued repository observations lose sidebar restoration authority when closeView disconnects their owner. Failed owned preflight schedules one coalesced ordinary recovery after FIFO release; failure of that recovery cannot self-retry. Non-removal admission reports typed eligibility rather than removal consent. Repair preparation is read-only and the removed direct-repair API cannot bypass approval. Passive sidebar restoration suppresses navigation before any content is mounted and restores canonical checkout/reference identity rather than row numbers. Closed owners reject direct rebuild/selection and late Forge choices as well as queued KVO. Background inventory reads preserve settled header appearance and accessibility; only initial loading or a changed settled result updates the header. Initial History mounting belongs to window initialization and cannot depend on passive selection callbacks. Closed sidebars reject navigation, repository opening, checkout, row mutation and remote actions. Header fallback uses actual snapshot staleness; capability recovery never restores obsolete unsupported guidance. A native spinner appears only before the first snapshot. Header state is evaluated outside rendering and identical presentations preserve rows and accessibility.
contracts.rootCause: A stale callback or cached action can replace a newer selection or apply obsolete content. A prune confirmation detached from current registration identity can forget worktrees the user did not approve. Restoring a row without its selection notification leaves controls stale; treating worktree rows only as lifecycle actions loses retained reference actions. Rebuilding an action from current owners or checking visibility alone lets old callbacks and deferred clicks regain authority after replacement or reopening. Comparing history state as ownership revokes harmless consent; a first-branch lookup redirects duplicate-row actions, and passive checked-out-branch following can override another checkout's selected history. Removal discards history and therefore cannot use history-insensitive repair ownership consent. Old ordinary reads can otherwise overwrite a newer preflight. Retrying a consumed preview replaces the original failure with a token error.

Exercise unsupported, capability checking, supported read, freshness and closure with and without retained rows; only initial work shows progress, and supported reads cannot revive unsupported guidance.

Explicit raw commit objects give alpha-sort-old and zeta-sort-new contrasting timestamps; assert actual displayed reference order, retained closed rows/selection/revision, unchanged HEAD, persisted mode, notification count and real responder routing. Keep independently named live and closed controls with shared setup.

contracts.invariant: Successful chunks are reconciled before controls recover, including failure paths. Busy commit submissions refuse immediately without enqueuing, while background Git commands retain FIFO order. Owned worktree reconciliation preserves pending invalidations; failure leaves the previous snapshot stale and earns one recovery read, with later events/manual refresh retryable and no automatic retry loop.
contracts.rootCause: Early return or premature idle publication leaves the displayed index and operation eligibility untruthful.

tests.oracle: Observe parsed components and main-thread completion.
Inspect actual staged first chunk and reconciled UI after second-chunk failure.
Controls recover only after authoritative reconciliation, preserving hook failure.
A duplicate click during reconciliation produces one staging result and no error notification.
A synchronous checkout is refused while the shared repository writer owns a staging operation.
Busy menus and stale reference/stash invocations preserve HEAD, worktree and stashes; a real Git failure still presents its error after admission recovers.
Hold the writer queue before execution; synchronous work is refused without running, queued completion releases ownership, and the coordinator accepts the next write.
Reconciliation and submission each reject a main-thread writer without launching it while read output remains available.
Before releasing the held writer, observe exactly one refusal, no hook or commit-message write and unchanged HEAD; retry after idle commits the original message.
The existing background Git command still executes after previously queued staging.
Deliver real Git report failure to the live owner, preserve administrative state, show no confirmation, and allow the following real preview.
Deliver the first real Remove failure after admission in live and replaced owners; route the error only to its origin, perform no force retry, and prove following writer progress.
Change Reclaim evidence to proven links, require another Repair click, then present a real Git writer failure while preserving links, HEAD/index/refs and FIFO progress.

Release the original controller while its admitted Remove awaits a real dirty-checkout refusal; prove deallocation before completion, no error/force presentation or writer cancellation, exact Git/index/content preservation and following FIFO writer progress.

A gated probe coalesces identical executable requests while a different executable completes.
An explicit unsupported protocol result launches once across repeated requests.

contracts.invariant: Completion preserves exit status and accepted bytes, while genuinely incomplete drainage stays explicit. Checked worktree writers retain their service, repository, task, canonical execution context and FIFO admission through terminal reconciliation. Closure and preference changes cancel queued work and reads while admitted writes and their operation-owned reconciliation finish; completion and admission release occur exactly once, including late callbacks and reconciliation failures. Native verification captures every output byte before independently mirroring it to the console; console backpressure cannot stall child completion or watchdogs. Log destinations stay inside configured verification artifacts, and capture/write/flush failures preserve the child status in diagnostics while failing verification. Console completeness is retained beside the raw log without writing synchronously to the merged console pipe. Managed Debug apps install optional stderr capture before NSApplicationMain, using invocation-owned cache storage and unique PID/UUID files. Unavailable capture preserves original stderr and emits finite warning metadata without crashing the app or changing an otherwise successful command status. Complete records use exclusive same-directory rename without replacing evidence; publication failures retain their finite operation and original errno. Required progress initialization is transactional and precedes command launch and reporting workers; a missing authenticated bundle-start record cannot pass even when the child exits zero. XCTest observers in both test bundles emit invocation/session/bundle-specific startup records independently of capture; ordinary application, Git or console text cannot establish managed native startup. Release production apps contain no capture hook. One managed supervisor owns startup, incremental native archival and the canonical console capture; one bounded worker writes the console. Native source discovery is fair and bounded, and accepted startup is cached. Fully archived unchanged scratch retires only after root and inherited writer leases release; incomplete, live or redirected sources stay registered and protected, and interrupted retirement remains recoverable; incomplete native collection remains explicit and optional. Native logging-only characterization contains no raw stderr write after pipe saturation and does not assume platform-dependent logging must block. Preset and raw entrypoints retain one authoritative xcodebuild console log and configure the same supervisor for native deadlines and console capture. Queued native startup evidence is observed before the startup-deadline verdict, matching command-output event handling when a selector wakeup crosses the boundary. Full native correctness and fresh analysis run in independent CI jobs with unchanged 75-minute limits. Correctness, analysis and worktree contracts depend only on toolchain smoke. The existing required unit tests and analyzer check runs after all three jobs and accepts only three successful dependency results including cancelled runs, rejecting failure, cancellation and skipped or missing dependency results. Only the small required aggregate and its result step use always(); expensive work remains cancellable; artifact uploads retain always(). Independent full UI, native regression and performance steps remain eligible after focused failures unless cancelled; failures remain blocking and artifact upload always runs. Distribution cleanup validates inventory structure and all mountpoints, then validates detach identities only for the exact owned image. Identified unrelated file or RAM images cannot block cleanup through irrelevant device metadata. Missing identity, malformed mountpoints, foreign occupancy and ambiguous owned devices remain unknown and retain staging; failed attachment cleanup and publication rollback remain protected by the required static script suite. Independent follow-on plans require successful prerequisite setup, including when an earlier verification step fails; failed, skipped or missing readiness cannot launch them. Workflow guards describe source and predicate coverage, not hosted execution evidence. Invocation leases validate the owned parent before a nonblocking regular-file open; rejected leases preserve exact failure causes and release all descriptors. Native infrastructure status is selected from child state observed before supervisor termination, never a positive exit induced by stopping the child. Exclusive rename has one syscall implementation with explicit parent-sync policy. Deferred native retirement keeps cleanup partial and its queue pending, including registration-storage failure; only a later authorized eligible cleanup retries it. PR #104 follow-up cleanup distinguishes retryable deferred retirement from retained evidence: incomplete or unverifiable sources remain protected without permanently blocking unrelated eligible cleanup. Explicit retry is required after retained evidence is repaired. Per-invocation publishers serialize and compare current records, preserve monotonic retirement proof, and never overwrite completed state with stale checkpoints. Hashes run outside broad proof leases; current authorization protects mutation boundaries.
contracts.rootCause: Leader exit is mistaken for EOF; arbitrary reader cutoffs truncate finite streams or hide descendant output. Treating a presentation cancellation as writer cancellation can terminate Git mid-write; shared discovery cancellation can also erase a completed write's reconciliation and release the queue too early. Serial independent native checks can exhaust a shared job limit before fresh analysis finishes. Validating irrelevant device metadata before establishing image ownership can strand packaging; ignoring unknown identity or mountpoint conflicts can instead authorize unsafe cleanup.

tests.oracle: Compare complete bytes from slow finite readers.
Observe descendant output released after the parent exits.
Repeated drainage cannot upgrade an incomplete stream to complete EOF.
A controlled peer exit between reads preserves its final acknowledgement.
The failure reason retains diagnostics written just before exit.
Injected application resource failures preserve caller descriptors and the successful control reaps its child.
Only a positive syscall write makes commit publication uncertain.
Actual Git writes are reconciled before completion and FIFO release, then a following real writer advances.
A completed real writer's failed reread remains an explicit GitX error with its underlying cause, then the queue advances.
Closure and preference changes leave an admitted task running; captured-context reconciliation completes before the following actual writer.
Closure and preference changes do not cancel post-write reconciliation or release the queue before terminal completion.
A closed service drains its active writer with exactly-once completion and release while preserving its last published snapshot.
A closed owner retains its post-write read and FIFO lease until completion, then rejects late publication and duplicate release.
Retain a terminal task callback after a document-owned operation completes; weak repository and service references must release.

Observe the actual held utility phase and independent main actor progress; reserve FIFO before capture, then await the service main-result acknowledgement before checking exact delivery and following real-writer progress or deleting fixtures.

Hold the actual evidence worker, cancel once, and prove early Cocoa completion, weak completion-owner release and following real-writer progress while still held; then await the actual main-result discard acknowledgement and require unchanged completion/preparation counts and Git state before teardown.
Use the default document-owned service and distinct executable proxies to prove both the admitted write and its reconciliation run the captured canonical Git after preferences change.
Cancel the report task through both Swift and Cocoa errors while its owner stays current; require Cocoa cancellation, exactly-once completion, unchanged metadata and subsequent FIFO progress.

Deliver both Swift and Cocoa cancellation errors from the operation-owned initial discovery while its owner stays live; require one Cocoa cancellation completion, no report or prune launch, exact Git metadata preservation, and one following real writer in FIFO order.
After explicit scope approval, hold the repair writer and verify a following unlock remains blocked through write and reconciliation.
Hold the final validation worker, replace or close its owner, acknowledge the late result once and prove the following request advances without any repair or filesystem changes.
Failed and truncated preflight reads never remove the checkout, preserve bytes, and release the next queued writer.
Cancel an owned removal read, deliver retained late callbacks, and prove exactly-once completion, no removal, and following-service progress.
Replace the selected executable during preflight; context validation rejects removal and preserves real repository metadata and checkout bytes.

Carry optional capture and complete startup ownership into empty launch environments. Required static fixtures enforce warnings-as-errors probe compilation, exact structured startup identities, no child launch or reporting worker on required setup failure, fail-closed early success without startup, and unchanged genuine failure/interruption status. Actual preset/raw shell fixtures use one supervisor and canonical console capture. Native fixtures cover binary checkpoints before close, fair bounded reads, a single console writer, inherited writer leases, identity conflicts, incomplete archives and resumable quarantine retirement. The actual aggregate shell accepts only all-success across all 125 terminal-result combinations, while source guards require always() on both the small aggregate and result step. Existing independent setup/cancellation predicates and packaging fixtures remain required. These authored checks do not establish hosted scheduling or execution evidence. PR #103 follow-up fixtures distinguish running children that exit positive, zero or by signal during termination from preexisting positive failures, for both native failure categories, and preserve cancellation with before/after child metadata. Shared rename fixtures cover both callers, collisions, platform unavailability, exact syscall errno, requested parent syncing and descriptor closure after sync failure. Actual cleanup fixtures retain the pending token and persist partial reports for held native leases, protected sources and retryable retirement/storage failures; after release a later eligible cleanup retires only the proven duplicate and can complete, while a newer pending token survives. Historical unmarked artifacts remain outside native adoption. PR #104 retirement follow-ups exercise post-deletion registration failure and later authorized completion, legacy prepared recovery only with intact owned archive evidence, missing/unprepared or redirected sources, and registration-directory fsync failure before deletion. The deletion phase survives deferred outcome reporting; absent paths alone never authorize cleanup. Canonical console flush/close/metadata failures return 74 while retaining the actual child exit code; prior interruption and blockers keep their status. A fresh tracker rejects foreign startup evidence, while an authenticated startup remains observed after record retirement. Preset/raw step receipts retain the exact supervisorCommand separately from the child command without nesting supervisors. Optional capture publication uses an authenticated capture-only fallback record with exact operation/category/errno, never the original stderr pipe. Swift warnings-as-errors probes cover fallback failure and continued startup; supervisor fixtures reject foreign or malformed records, archive valid warnings, and never accept fallback capture as XCTest startup. CI structure protection names each expensive job and its toolchain-smoke prerequisite instead of counting dependency strings; the aggregate still requires correctness, analysis and worktree-contract success. Workflow source fixtures do not establish hosted scheduling evidence. PR #104 follow-up subprocesses release a naturally exiting child during diagnostic collection; preserve a positive result sampled before the first termination signal, retain failure-entry and pre-signal observations, and keep termination-handler exits subordinate to infrastructure status. Durable exclusive rename syncs both distinct parents, deduplicates a shared parent, and preserves destination-sync errno. Further PR #104 script regressions require nonblocking retained outcomes for incomplete/missing evidence, no default rehash of retained records, explicit CLI retry after repair, fresh registration reads after inventory, cross-process publisher exclusion, compare-and-publish refusal, no stale downgrade after publication failure, restrictive nonregular/symlink/ownership checks with descriptor closure, no hash before a held writer-lease check, and no global proof lease while hashing. Per-subtest registration restoration runs in finally. Existing newer-token and specific-reason assertions remain exact. Audit registrations are preserved; metadata discovery remains linear and does not establish a measured timing improvement.
Hold the real shared writer, observe busy state, explicitly release it, and require quiescence without creating a mutation service.
Use the production observer attachment factory with binary input, symlink and nonregular candidates; require a bounded tail attachment, preserve source bytes and handle absent capture.
Publish two actual atomic records, decode both complete payloads, require distinct names and no pending files, and preserve preexisting evidence byte-for-byte.
Unsupported JSON cannot leave pending or complete evidence.
Inject ENOSPC during writing and EACCES during publication; preserve the exact finite operation and errno and remove incomplete records.
Preserve an existing final record on EEXIST, retry EINTR and partial writes, decode the complete new record and remove pending files.
Take retained startup publication failure once before recursive observer delivery; preserve errno.
Assert exact binary crash/sanitizer tail bytes, no duplicate range, newly appended bytes, independent case state and 64 KiB per-excerpt/256 KiB per-case budgets without modifying original logs.
Hold the real shared invocation lease, require exclusive acquisition to fail, release its owner and acquire exclusively.

Inject parent/lease inspection and ownership failures, open exhaustion and lock contention; assert typed operation/category/errno, closed descriptors, nonblocking flags and unchanged evidence. Actual native subprocess fixtures additionally reject FIFO, symlink, directory and absent leases within a bounded backstop; authored protection is not execution evidence. Capture syscall result and errno before XCTest assertions. The retirement queue fixture creates a distinct commit and queues its token after the proof lease releases; cleanup identifies the newer token explicitly and cannot clear it.
A missing invocation root retains the open-lease-directory operation and ENOENT.

Snapshot existing log identities and lengths before a case. Unchanged prior launches consume no budget; new launches precede growing existing logs, appended bytes are retained once, binary bytes and source files remain intact. Compiled native probes additionally place five alphabetically earlier logs before a current crashing launch and require the current tail first.

contracts.invariant: Rendered and exported diagnostics redact credentials across every chunk/cutoff boundary while preserving ordinary URLs. Public worktree lifecycle diagnostics contain finite operation, phase and rejection categories plus counts; raw Git arguments, output, lock reasons, branch names and filesystem paths never enter those public events. Sensitive diagnostic details use existing redaction and private visibility while execution and authorization evidence stay raw. Each terminal lifecycle failure has one logging owner preserving its actual phase and finite category; removal consent rejection uses consent. Non-removal inventory admission uses typed eligibility reasons and the finite eligibility category, distinct from removal approval and executable context failures.
contracts.rootCause: Truncating before redaction or parsing only common userinfo shapes can expose secrets. Interpolating full lifecycle arguments or failed output publicly exposes user-authored lock reasons and repository details.

tests.oracle: Ordinary URLs and subsequent diagnostics remain byte-faithful.
Every two-part split excludes the credential from output.
Both summary cutoff and full export exclude secrets.
Malformed userinfo stays redacted through the application boundary.
Dotted usernames and numeric password prefixes remain hidden across chunks.

After real service routes, poll fresh current-process OSLog snapshots on one utility task with 0/250/500/1000ms backoff, a monotonic retry deadline and propagated query errors; require both exact positive events and reject every raw argument, output and lock-reason canary in the same successful snapshot.
Inspect the actual underlying eligibility error and emitted finite terminal category for each invalid lock/unlock target; no removal-consent event or writer is permitted.

contracts.invariant: An export error survives temporary invisibility and is discarded only after actual owner dismissal.
contracts.rootCause: Visibility is confused with lifetime, causing lost errors or presentation on a closed owner.

tests.oracle: Observe actual owned artifact, destination and restored control.
Hide/minimize then restore; exactly one error is presented.
Closed or detached owners receive no later error.

contracts.invariant: Tests and explicit-checkout Git inspection isolate inherited repository selectors while retaining configured local hooks and binary input. Presentation fixtures retain files through cancellation and main-actor worker acknowledgement, restore the original Git preference once, then remove only drained fixtures. Explicit presentation-fixture opens establish the existing host as active and its visible owner window or sheet as key before queue actions; later production resumption remains focus-preserving. Cleanup Git fixtures suppress automatic maintenance and GC under isolated configuration so detached writers cannot race read-only snapshot assertions. Fingerprinting still rejects entries removed after enumeration. Maintenance and GC suppression are persisted in cleanup fixture and dependency repositories, covering independent Git invocations as well as helper calls. History auxiliary hook directories stay outside watched content, are registered with the fixture, restore literal hooks configuration and retain fixture-owned fallback cleanup.
contracts.rootCause: Ambient repositories, config, hooks and identity make tests pass against the wrong state. Preference notifications during teardown can restart services, while premature fixture deletion races late workers. Detached Git auto-maintenance can change a fixture after its commit has returned.

tests.oracle: Inspect isolated Git environment and preserved non-Git variables.
Real Git commits preserve explicitly configured fixture hooks.
Compare exact binary stdin bytes.
Hold an actual discovery worker; cleanup must remain pending with its files present until the late worker result is acknowledged on main.
At the actual single preference-restoration boundary, both real fixture roots still exist and all services are drained; afterward the original preference is restored and both roots are absent.
Hide the test application, explicitly open a fixture, and require the same existing host to be active with a visible key owner before starting queue assertions.
Remove a normal auxiliary directory explicitly; retain a directory through a thrown scope, release its fixture owner and assert actual filesystem removal.
Observe the shared writer without scheduling work, close before its initial callback drains, and require no callback and no busy writer.

Query required Objective-C selectors in the running Debug host.

Exercise the imported task and configuration-dependent runtime surface in Release.

Query actual Objective-C instance methods in Release: fixture hooks, drainage and repair harness selectors are absent, while production compatibility selectors remain available.

Runtime queries require both removed direct-repair selectors and the obsolete begin-repair fixture bridge to be absent; production repair preparation and confirmation remain available.

Query the actual capture bootstrap runtime class and entry selector, requiring Debug presence and Release absence.

Inspect the actual current-invocation XCTest bundle-start record; explicit registration calls cannot substitute for an already-published automatic startup record.

contracts.family: UI fixture isolation and Finder metadata
contracts.invariant: UI fixture repositories ignore untracked Finder metadata while preserving real untracked files, explicitly tracked metadata and existing exclusion rules. Isolated fixture homes create independent preferences directories and remain owned by workspace cleanup in every consuming test target.
